contract: C4 (blocked) and C5 (the guard and blocked), docs/protocol.md, since board ab-v16.33 (part 1c of the per-scope build). The receiver guards and sends blocked so; the daemon reads blocked (agentwatch's part 3: the Browser page names the repo of the scope, and the operator's allow prompt names from). Every value is a sample.
noticesNote: Each msg is a blocked notice as the receiver sends it on the daemon's socket (C4): tab, host, scope (the tab's scope when the notice goes, or null for a tab of no scope) and from (the tab's last listed host, or null). Its fields come in this order.

notices.note: A tab of a scope, on a site of its list, at a host of no list (for example a sign-in provider that a site's link opens): scope names the repo whose list lacks the host, from names the site where the tab was.
The guard sent a tab of a scope away from another scope's site (a service worker's page): its from stays the last listed host, never the blocked one.
A new popup with no commit of its own: from is its opener's last listed host.
A tab of no scope (an operator's tab, marked or not, a tab of the orphan set, the restore tab) has scope null; a tab with no listed host yet (for example a new tab at about:blank) has from null.

guardNote: C5's guard (layers 2 and 3). in: the fields of the last set_scopes (null: none since the worker's start). tab: what the tab is: scope (its scope in the map), marked (the operator mark), orphan (in the orphan set), restore (the domain of the running import whose restore tab it is), or {} (a tab of no scope, not marked). url: the URL of a main-frame onBeforeNavigate or onCommitted. host: the host that the guard judges (an http:/https: URL's, or a blob: URL's inner origin's; null: no check). blocks: the host is not in the tab's covered set, so the receiver sends the tab to about:blank and sends blocked with this host. C5's closing rule and the import's close (C6) judge a tab's page by the same host (a blob: page by its inner origin).

guard.note: A tab of a scope, at a host of its list (a subdomain too): no check fails, the page stays.
The worker hole: a tab of scope md-lead at a site of scope v-lead's list (a worker of that site can answer with no request). The guard sends the tab to about:blank and sends blocked.
A host of no list.
A port does not count: the host does.
A blob: URL is judged by its inner origin's host: another scope's site.
A blob: URL of a site of the tab's list stays.
A blob: URL of an opaque origin has no host: no check (its page has no site's cookies or storage).
about:blank, data: and chrome: URLs have no host: no check.
The New Tab page of a marked tab: no check.
A scope whose list is none (an ended session's null): every host is off its list.
A scope that scopes does not name has the default list.
A scope that scopes does not name, with default null: no list.
A tab of no scope that is not marked (an operator's unmarked tab, the page of a finished import): the union of the lists.
A tab of no scope that is not marked, at a host of no list.
A marked tab with the operator value "*": every host.
A marked tab with a list name: that list only (Receiver.tabList).
A marked tab with a list name, at a host of that list.
A marked tab with no operator value (null): no host.
A tab of the orphan set: no host, also one on the union of the lists.
The restore tab of a running import: its domain (rules 6 and 7), whatever the lists hold.
The restore tab of a running import: no other host, also one on the union of the lists.
A set_scopes that is not applied (scopes is not an object): C4 gives every scope no list, so the guard fails closed with the scope rules.
A set_scopes that is not applied: a tab of no scope still has the union of the lists that apply.
Before the first set_scopes after the worker's start (in: null): no tab has a list, except the restore tab.
A refused entry (not a normalized entry) is on no list.
